text: In Genesis 22 there arises a question to which no answer is supplied. Abraham receives the command to take his son, his only son, whom he loves; yet of the feeling with which he receives it no account is offered, nor does the narrator describe any inward motion of his mind. He makes no protest, and he enters into no bargaining over the command. Of the Abraham who argued for Sodom there is here no sign; he is put before us less as a character than as a silence, and that silence is the chief matter of the chapter.
